article_content: After a century of dormancy, a forgotten campsite from Captain Robert Scott's Antarctic expedition has been rediscovered. Prof. Clive Oppenheimer of Cambridge University located the site using original expedition documents. Used by surviving members of Scott's 1910-13 team, it marks their scientific work on Mount Erebus where geologist Frank Debenham first envisioned a polar research institution. Though Scott's party reached the South Pole in 1912 only to find Amundsen's team had preceded them, their tragic return journey claimed all five lives. Today, the camp's sole remains are stone circles that once secured tents - a silent testament to human endurance. Collaborative preservation efforts between UK and New Zealand authorities aim to protect this historic site, honoring both the triumphs and tragedies of early Antarctic exploration.

Prof. Clive Oppenheimer tare da cikin Universite Cambridjga ya samun yake da cikin abincin na soɗo ayyuka da na son wani masu rana. Ayyuka ta fiyahi da masu bayanin daɗi a cikin jihimi da 1912 ya fiyahi da yadda ayyuka Scott. Kuyyade, labarai a yau yaƙoyin Mount Erebus ya samun yake da ƙasare da Frank Debenham, na sona ya kamar daidaita ake kawoƙƙalbin ake daidaita labari. Suna ƙawoƙƙalbin ya ke daidai da Roald Amundsen na 1912, amma daɗin yake a cikin labarai, sabon masu bayanin ya yin zuciya. article_content: One of Europe’s busiest airports temporarily closed its new runway Wednesday after a commercial aircraft veered off a taxiway during post-landing maneuvers. KLM Royal Dutch Airlines Flight KL1831, arriving from Nairobi, Kenya, departed the designated path while taxiing toward the terminal shortly after landing. Despite the deviation, no injuries occurred and the Boeing 747-400 came to rest with its nose wheels embedded in grassy terrain. Passengers reported receiving an in-cabin announcement explaining brake system irregularities caused the incident. Eyewitness Vincent Verweij shared images on social media showing the aircraft’s precarious position, noting the cabin remained calm until ground staff arrived approximately one hour later. Schiphol officials rerouted incoming flights to alternate runways until technicians cleared the obstruction. Investigations into the brake malfunction continue as authorities assess operational impacts.

article_content: The UK government has announced a £15 billion road infrastructure package covering over 100 projects by 2021. Prime Minister David Cameron framed the initiative as reviving Margaret Thatcher's 1989 'roads for prosperity' strategy, positioning it as the most significant road development since Roman times. Key components include constructing a tunnel for the A303 near Stonehenge, upgrading the A1 motorway north of Newcastle, and enhancing trans-Pennine routes. Critics argue the plan risks damaging ecologically sensitive areas and historic sites while neglecting public transport needs. Proponents highlight economic growth potential, though opponents point to unmet past commitments and concerns over increased traffic congestion. The announcement comes amid ongoing debates about infrastructure funding priorities and delivery timelines.

article_content: Cairo, Egypt (CNN) — Wael Ghonim, an Egyptian activist celebrated by protesters as a hero, directly addressed the nation's leaders Wednesday: 'If you are true Egyptians, if you are heroic Egyptians, it’s time to step down.' Ghonim, released Monday after a 10-day detention by Egyptian authorities, stated negotiations with President Hosni Mubarak’s regime were 'no longer viable.' Highlighting over 300 protest-related deaths documented by Human Rights Watch—including 232 in Cairo—he demanded accountability: 'The president must resign for this crime.' Organizing protests since January 25 via a pivotal Facebook page, Ghonim revealed strategic shifts from nonviolent negotiation to mass mobilization. Despite his role as Head of Marketing for Google Middle East/North Africa and安稳 family life in Dubai, he declared readiness to sacrifice everything for reform. Challenging Vice President Omar Suleiman, he vowed: 'Kill us if you can—we reclaim this country!' His public empowerment transfer to his wife underscored resolve. Ghonim emphasized youth-led, decentralized activism inspired by 'V for Vendetta,' rejecting claims of Muslim Brotherhood involvement. While acknowledging Mubarak’s past contributions, he insisted systemic change required dissolving the National Democratic Party. Military intervention replaced police after initial violent crackdowns, creating relative calm.

article_content: Seventeen-year-old Adam Pickup was found deceased two days after vanishing during a nighttime outing. Authorities suspect exposure as the likely cause of death. His body was discovered under a railway structure near Manchester's Deansgate station, clad only in a shirt and jeans. Surveillance footage captured him last on Oxford Street at 3:30 AM Saturday following a visit to Fab Cafe. Located Monday afternoon within 0.5 miles of his disappearance point, no suspicious evidence was found. Family announced the tragic news via social media, expressing gratitude for community support. Over 18,000 individuals honored him on a memorial page. After releasing two suspects without charges, police stated no foul play indications. A post-mortem examination is pending as locals observed a moment's silence during New Year's Eve festivities.

article_content: Twitter is introducing its 'Offers' feature to bridge social media and in-store shopping. Merchants can post discounts directly to users' feeds, redeemable via linked cards at checkout. Users save offers to their cards instantly and receive automatic savings upon payment. The encrypted card data remains accessible for removal anytime. Initially limited to the U.S., the feature will trial with holiday-season partners. This initiative builds on Twitter’s e-commerce efforts, including its recent 'Buy' button integration. With 284 million monthly users (23% annual growth), the platform seeks new revenue avenues as online shopping expands.
